```markdown
## lock-closures-roadmap — 2026-11-06

- [ ] Closure email notices to boat operators (was Stage 2, Track B, O5).
      Email every address on an operator mailing list within an hour of a
      new entry in the closure log's live feed. Text-message notices were
      out of scope.
      Size: small (one closure-log poll every 10 minutes)
      Done when: a notice job and its operator mailing list exist, and in a
      test an email reaches every address within an hour of a new closure entry.

- [ ] 7-day closure-risk outlook per lock (was Track A Ranked list #1, O2).
      Feed the river-level forecast through the Stage 1 closure-response
      curve (specs/lock-closures-stage-1-findings.md).
      Size: small (one model run a day; Stage 1's fit took 22 min on 1.8 GB)
      Done when: a 7-day closure-risk outlook for each lock is produced from
      the river-level forecast.

- [ ] Per-lock closure curves pooled across all 14 locks (was Track A Ranked list #2, O3).
      Stage 1 found that the four locks with the longest records share close
      to the same curve.
      Size: large (about 14× Stage 1's 1.8 GB)
      Done when: separate closure curves for all 14 locks, pooled across
      locks, are fit on real data.

- [ ] Closure-history map for boat operators (was Track A Ranked list #3, O4).
      Size: about a day (one static map page)
      Done when: operators can open a map of each lock's closure history.
```

```
Edit specs/lock-closures-roadmap.md

Stage 1's findings file stays in `specs/` as the study's result. There are no methodology or critique files to retire, because this roadmap had no spec.

**4. Commit on `main`**

git add specs/deferred_items.md specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md
git commit -m "Park lock-closures roadmap (1 of 2 stages complete): funding ended"
```

Afterwards, the only open work for this project will be the four backlog items. If funding returns, any of them can be promoted through `/deferred`. Stage 1's result stays on record: closures rise steeply above a gauge level of 3.1 m.
